info.title: Firefox + OpenOffice Writer + File Explorer - Computer Use Agent Skill
info.description: Instructions for a computer use agent to use Mozilla Firefox, OpenOffice Writer, and File Explorer on Windows to download a PDF, extract text, and save it to the desktop.

steps: Click the search bar on the Windows taskbar (bottom of screen)
Type 'Firefox'
Click 'Mozilla Firefox' in the search results
Wait for Firefox to fully load (address bar becomes interactive)
Maximize the Firefox window if not already maximized
Take ONE screenshot to confirm Firefox is open

visualCues.addressBar: Located at the top of the window, shows 'Search or enter web address'
visualCues.mainArea: Large browser viewport below the address bar

x-agent-instructions.verification: Screenshot should show Firefox address bar at top and a new tab page or homepage

post.summary: Navigate to a URL in Mozilla Firefox

steps: Click on the address bar at the top of the Firefox window (it shows the current URL or 'Search or enter web address')
Press Ctrl+A to select any existing text in the address bar
Type the full URL: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/pdfs/whitepapers/latest/aws-overview/aws-overview.pdf
Press Enter to navigate
Wait for the page to fully load — for a PDF this may take 10-20 seconds
Take ONE screenshot to confirm the page/PDF has loaded

visualCues.addressBar: Top center of Firefox window, shows current URL after navigation
visualCues.loadingIndicator: Spinning icon in the browser tab while loading
visualCues.pdfLoaded: PDF viewer renders inside Firefox with toolbar showing Download, Print, Zoom controls at top

tips: If the page shows a loading spinner, wait before taking a screenshot
Firefox has a built-in PDF viewer — the PDF will render directly in the browser tab
If a security warning appears, click 'Continue' or 'Keep' to proceed

post.summary: Download the PDF from Firefox's built-in PDF viewer

steps: Once the PDF is loaded in Firefox, look for the Firefox PDF toolbar that appears at the TOP of the PDF viewer
The PDF toolbar contains icons: Download (arrow pointing down), Print, Rotate, Fit to page, Zoom in/out
Click the Download icon (downward arrow icon) in the PDF toolbar — it is typically in the top-right area of the PDF viewer toolbar
Alternatively, press Ctrl+Shift+S to open the Save As dialog
A download notification will appear at the bottom or top-right of the Firefox window
Wait for the download to complete — the notification will show 'Open file' when done
Note the download location: by default files go to the Downloads folder (C:\Users\<username>\Downloads)
Take ONE screenshot to confirm the download completed

alternativeMethod.description: If the PDF toolbar is not visible, hover over the top of the PDF to reveal it, or use the Firefox menu
steps: Click the '...' (More actions) button in the top-right of Firefox
Click 'Save page as...' or press Ctrl+S
In the Save As dialog, note the save location and filename
Click Save

visualCues.pdfToolbar: Thin toolbar overlaid at the top of the PDF content area with small icons
visualCues.downloadButton: Arrow pointing downward icon, usually on the right side of the PDF toolbar
visualCues.downloadComplete: Notification bar at top or bottom of Firefox, or Downloads panel showing file with checkmark

tips: The PDF file is named 'aws-overview.pdf' by default
Downloads go to C:\Users\<username>\Downloads unless changed
You can also right-click the PDF page and look for 'Save as' option
If download bar appears at the top of Firefox (newer versions), click the download icon there

post.summary: Read the PDF in Firefox and find the AWS Bedrock section

steps: With the PDF open in Firefox, use Ctrl+F to open the Find toolbar
Type 'Bedrock' in the Find box and press Enter
Firefox will highlight and jump to the first occurrence of 'Bedrock' in the PDF
Use the Find navigation arrows (next/previous) to find the most relevant section describing AWS Bedrock as a service
Look for a section heading like 'Amazon Bedrock' or content that describes what Bedrock does
Once you locate the relevant section, take a screenshot to see the text on screen
Read the visible text carefully from the screenshot
If the section continues off-screen, scroll down using Page Down or the scroll wheel to see more text
Take screenshots of each portion of the Bedrock section until you have captured all the relevant descriptive text
Close the Find toolbar by pressing Escape
Mentally note or record all the text you need to copy
Click at the very beginning of the Bedrock section text in the PDF
Hold Shift and click at the end of the section you want to copy, OR
Use Ctrl+A to select all text (not recommended for large PDFs — use click-drag instead)
For a specific section: click at start of text, hold Shift, click at end of desired text
Press Ctrl+C to copy the selected text
The text is now in the clipboard

tips: PDF text selection in Firefox works like a normal web page — click and drag to select
The Bedrock section may be titled 'Amazon Bedrock' and describe it as a managed service for foundation models
If text selection is difficult (e.g., scanned PDF), you may need to read and manually retype key content
Prioritize the descriptive paragraphs that explain what Amazon Bedrock is and what it does
The AWS Overview whitepaper organizes services by category — look in the 'Machine Learning' section for Bedrock
Use Ctrl+F and search for 'Amazon Bedrock' (full name) for best results
x-agent-instructions.verification: Screenshot should show highlighted search result for 'Bedrock' in the PDF

steps: Press the Windows key or click the search bar on the taskbar
Type 'OpenOffice Writer'
Click 'OpenOffice Writer' in the search results
OpenOffice Writer will open with a blank document
Maximize or resize the Writer window so it is clearly visible
Take ONE screenshot to confirm Writer is open

visualCues.mainArea: Large blank white text area below a thin menu bar
visualCues.menuBar: File, Edit, Format, View, Help menus at the top

tips: OpenOffice Writer is a document editor — no formatting is preserved from PDF
The cursor will be at the top-left of the blank document by default
If Writer was previously open, it may have content — use Ctrl+A then Delete to clear it

post.summary: Paste extracted text into OpenOffice Writer

steps: Click inside the Writer document area to ensure it has focus
If there is existing text, press Ctrl+A to select all, then press Delete to clear it
Optionally type a header line like 'AWS Bedrock Overview' followed by two newlines for organization
Press Ctrl+V to paste the copied text from the clipboard
Take ONE screenshot to verify the text has been pasted correctly
Review the pasted text to confirm it contains the Bedrock section content
tips: If the clipboard text was copied from a PDF, formatting (bold, headers) will be lost — only plain text is pasted
Line breaks may differ from the PDF layout — this is expected behavior
If pasting results in garbled characters, the PDF may have used special encoding — manually type key content instead
x-agent-instructions.verification: Screenshot shows Writer document area populated with AWS Bedrock description text

post.summary: Save the Writer file to the Desktop

steps: Press Ctrl+S to open the Save As dialog (first time saving an untitled document)
The Save As dialog will open showing the current folder
In the left panel of the Save As dialog, look for 'Desktop' — click it to navigate to the Desktop
Alternatively, in the address bar of the Save As dialog, type 'Desktop' or navigate via the left sidebar
Click in the 'File name' field at the bottom of the dialog
Clear any existing filename text (triple-click or Ctrl+A)
Type exactly: aws-bedrock-overview
Ensure 'Save as type' dropdown shows 'ODF Text Document (*.odt)' — if not, change it
Click the 'Save' button
The window title should change to 'aws-bedrock-overview - OpenOffice Writer'

findDesktop: Method 1: Click 'Desktop' in the left Quick Access panel of the dialog
Method 2: Click the address bar in the dialog and type '%USERPROFILE%\Desktop' then press Enter
Method 3: Navigate to C:\Users\<username>\Desktop using the folder tree
saveAsDialogNavigation.filenameField: Located at the bottom of the Save As dialog, labeled 'File name:'
saveAsDialogNavigation.saveAsType: Set to 'ODF Text Document (*.odt)' — the .txt extension will be added automatically

visualCues.saveAsDialog: Standard Windows Save As file dialog with navigation panel on left, file list in center, filename field at bottom
visualCues.desktopShortcut: Desktop entry in the left Quick Access panel, usually near the top
visualCues.successIndicator: Writer title bar changes from 'Untitled 1 - OpenOffice Writer' to 'aws-bedrock-overview - OpenOffice Writer'

tips: Do NOT include '.txt' in the filename field — Windows adds it automatically based on the file type dropdown
If Writer asks 'Do you want to replace it?' a file already exists — click Yes to overwrite
After saving, the title bar confirms the filename and location
x-agent-instructions.verification: Screenshot shows Writer title bar reads 'aws-bedrock-overview - OpenOffice Writer'

methods.name: Alt+Tab
methods.description: Hold Alt, press Tab to cycle through open windows. Release Alt to switch to highlighted window.

methods.name: Taskbar click
methods.description: Click the application icon in the Windows taskbar at the bottom of the screen to bring it to focus.

methods.name: Windows key + number
methods.description: Press Win+1, Win+2, etc. to switch to the nth app in the taskbar.

tips: Use Alt+Tab to quickly switch between Firefox (PDF) and Writer
The taskbar at the bottom shows all open application windows as icons
If a window appears minimized, click its taskbar icon to restore it

post.summary: Recover from stuck states and unexpected dialogs

steps: Press Escape to close any open dialog or overlay
Press Alt+Tab to bring the correct application to the front
Take ONE screenshot to assess current state
Resume from the last successfully completed step

firefoxDownloadBar.description: Firefox shows a download bar at the top or a notification — interact with it to open or locate the file
firefoxDownloadBar.recovery: Click 'Open file' in the download notification, or navigate to Downloads folder

pdfNotLoading.description: PDF page shows blank or error
pdfNotLoading.recovery: Press F5 to refresh, or re-navigate to the URL

saveAsDialogNotNavigatingToDesktop.description: Cannot find Desktop in Save As dialog
saveAsDialogNotNavigatingToDesktop.recovery: Click the address bar in the Save As dialog, type Desktop, press Enter

textNotCopied.description: Paste in Writer results in nothing or wrong content
textNotCopied.recovery: Switch back to Firefox, re-select text in the PDF, press Ctrl+C again, switch to Writer, try Ctrl+V again

firefoxPdfToolbarHidden.description: PDF toolbar not visible in Firefox
firefoxPdfToolbarHidden.recovery: Move the mouse to the very top of the PDF content area to reveal the floating toolbar

applicationOverview.name: Microsoft Firefox + OpenOffice Writer + File Explorer
applicationOverview.type: Web Browser + Text Editor + File Manager
applicationOverview.purpose: Download a PDF from the web, extract specific text content, and save it as a plain text file on the Desktop

firefox.titleBar: Very top — shows tab titles and window controls (minimize, maximize, close)
firefox.tabBar: Below title bar — shows open tabs, new tab button (+)
firefox.addressBar: Below tab bar — shows current URL, navigation arrows (back/forward) on the left, settings icon (...) on right
firefox.pdfToolbar: Overlaid at top of PDF content area when a PDF is open — contains Download, Print, Rotate, Zoom controls
firefox.viewport: Main content area — renders the PDF or web page
firefox.downloadNotification: Appears at top-right or bottom of viewport when a file is downloading or downloaded

writer.titleBar: Top — shows filename and app name (e.g. 'Untitled 1 - OpenOffice Writer')
writer.menuBar: Below title bar — File, Edit, Format, View, Help menus
writer.textArea: Main body — large blank white area for typing/pasting text

saveAsDialog.navigationPanel: Left side — Quick Access (Desktop, Downloads, Documents), This PC, Network
saveAsDialog.fileList: Center — shows files and folders at current location
saveAsDialog.addressBar: Top of dialog — shows current path
saveAsDialog.filenameField: Bottom of dialog — text input labeled 'File name:'
saveAsDialog.saveAsTypeDropdown: Below filename field — controls file extension
saveAsDialog.saveButton: Bottom right — click to confirm save

coordinatePlanning.description: Take a screenshot after each major transition to orient coordinates. Identify key UI elements from their visual appearance and spatial position.
coordinatePlanning.firefoxAddressBar: Centered at the very top of the Firefox window, approximately y=50 on a maximized 1080p screen
coordinatePlanning.pdfToolbar: When PDF is open, toolbar appears at approximately y=130-150, spanning the width of the PDF content area
coordinatePlanning.writerDocumentArea: Occupies almost the entire window below the menu bar, starting at approximately y=50

guidelines: Navigate to URL → wait for load → THEN screenshot
Open Find (Ctrl+F) → type search term → navigate to result → THEN screenshot
Select text → Ctrl+C → switch to Writer → Ctrl+V → THEN screenshot
Ctrl+S → navigate to Desktop → type filename → Save → THEN screenshot
screenshotTriggers: After PDF finishes loading in Firefox
After locating the Bedrock section in the PDF (to read text)
After saving the file (to confirm title bar)

pdfInteractionNotes.firefoxPdfViewer: Firefox renders PDFs natively without requiring Adobe Reader. The PDF is interactive — you can click text, use Ctrl+F to search, and select/copy text.
pdfInteractionNotes.textSelection: Click and drag to select text in the PDF viewer, just like selecting text on a web page. Ctrl+A selects all text in the PDF.
pdfInteractionNotes.findInPdf: Ctrl+F opens the Find bar. Type 'Amazon Bedrock' or 'Bedrock' to jump to relevant sections.
pdfInteractionNotes.copyingFromPdf: After selecting text, Ctrl+C copies it to the clipboard. Paste into Writer with Ctrl+V.
pdfInteractionNotes.scrolling: Use mouse scroll wheel or Page Down/Page Up to navigate through the PDF. The scroll bar is on the right side of the PDF viewport.

firefoxNotLoading.recovery: Wait 15 seconds, then press F5 to refresh. If still failing, re-type the URL in the address bar.

pdfDownloadFailed.recovery: Press Ctrl+S in Firefox to trigger Save As for the currently open page

cannotSelectTextInPdf.cause: PDF may be image-based (scanned) rather than text-based
cannotSelectTextInPdf.recovery: Manually read the visible text from the screenshot and type it into Writer

clipboardEmpty.cause: Ctrl+C was not pressed after selecting text, or selection was lost
clipboardEmpty.recovery: Switch back to Firefox, reselect the Bedrock text, press Ctrl+C, switch back to Writer, press Ctrl+V

saveAsNoDesktopOption.cause: Desktop not visible in Quick Access panel
saveAsNoDesktopOption.recovery: In the Save As dialog address bar, type C:\Users\Public\Desktop or use the path %USERPROFILE%\Desktop

writerAlreadyHasContent.cause: Writer was already open with previous content
writerAlreadyHasContent.recovery: Press Ctrl+A to select all existing text, then Delete to clear it before pasting

firefoxPdfOpenedInAdobeOrOther.cause: Default PDF handler is not Firefox
firefoxPdfOpenedInAdobeOrOther.recovery: Right-click the downloaded PDF in File Explorer, select 'Open with' > 'Mozilla Firefox'

firefox.Ctrl+F: Open Find in page (works in PDF viewer)

workflowOrder: 2. Navigate to the AWS Overview PDF URL
3. Wait for PDF to load in Firefox's built-in viewer
4. Download the PDF using the Firefox PDF toolbar download button
5. Use Ctrl+F in the Firefox PDF viewer to search for 'Amazon Bedrock'
6. Navigate to the Bedrock section and read/screenshot the content
7. Select the relevant Bedrock text and press Ctrl+C to copy
9. Click in the Writer document area and press Ctrl+V to paste
10. Press Ctrl+S to open Save As dialog
11. Navigate to Desktop in the Save As dialog
13. Confirm Save as type is .txt and click Save
14. Verify the Writer title bar shows 'aws-bedrock-overview - OpenOffice Writer'
